judgment.explanation: 王大將軍 in the main text refers to Wang Dun (王敦), the rebel general who raised troops against the Jin emperor. The story describes Wang Dun's rebellion at 姑孰 and the emperor's reconnaissance. Candidate c0 (王敦) matches this historical referent. Candidate c1 (王隱) is a different person; the alias registry entry for 王大將軍 as 王隱 comes from a different story context (楊朗 story) and does not fit this narrative about the rebellion against 晉明帝.

assertions.interpretation: Wang Dun had already rebelled before the scene begins; this establishes the prior state that motivates the emperor's reconnaissance.
Wang Dun's army was stationed at Gushu at the time of the events, providing the location context for the scene.
Before reaching the camp, at a distance of over ten li, the emperor encountered the old woman's shop—a spatial-temporal point within the scene.
The emperor passed by and rested at the old woman's shop, a sequential event within the scene.
The emperor then gave the horsewhip to the old woman and departed—a sequential action within the scene.
The emperor circled Wang Dun's camp and came out—a sequential event within the scene after departing from the old woman.
Wang Dun ordered riders to pursue the emperor—a subsequent event within the scene.
By the time the pursuers set out, the emperor had already covered many li—indicating elapsed distance/time within the scene.
